To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The rats ran faster on the large reinforcement trails than on the small reinforcement trails.
the magnitude of reward and differential stimulus consequences affect the rate of running.

(1) rats will run more rapidly on a straight alley for a large reward than for a small reward; (2) this difference in speed is not due to a difference in the time taken to reach the goal box, but to a difference in running speed; (3) this difference in running speed is not due simply to the fact that the large reward is more attractive than the small reward, since the same difference in speed is found when the large reward is replaced by a neutral stimulus,
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the magnitude of reward upon the speed with which a rat runs a straight alley.
the effect of the magnitude of reward upon behavior.
the effects of the magnitude of reward upon the speed of response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a differential stimulus consequence is not a necessary and sufficient condition for the occurrence of differential instrumental behavior, and that a differential stimulus-consequence is not a necessary condition for the occurrence, or the maintenance, of differential instrumental behavior.

a large reward is associated with a high rate of running in a straight alley, a small reward is associated with low rate of running, and the magnitude of the stimulus consequences is related to the speed of running.
differential stimulus consequence is a necessary and sufficient condition for a stimulus consequence to be reinforcing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnitude of reward is a major factor in determining the speed with which a rat will run a straight alley.

the magnitude of reward has little effect on the rate of responding, and that the rate of response on the large reinforcement trial is not a function of the rate of response of the previous small reinforcement trial.
the magnitude of reward has a greater effect upon behavior than do differential stimulus consequences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnitude of reward matters. It is not enough to just give a reward, the size of that reward matters.
the magnitude of reinforcement is a critical variable in determining whether a rat learns to run faster or slower on a given reinforcement schedule.
the brain’s reward system is not a simple, single system that responds the same way to all rewards, but is instead composed of multiple systems that are tuned to different types of reward.
